sentences.text: There's a disturbing detail in this diplomatic room most people miss.
This is The Ambassadors, painted by Hans Holbein the Younger in 1533.
Two rich ambassadors stand beside a table stacked with instruments, showing off their knowledge.
A strange grey shape floats across the floor.
According to the National Gallery, Holbein painted a human skull skewed in extreme perspective.
Viewers should see a normal diplomatic meeting.
But a sinister shadow of death corrupts the room.
They display worldly wealth, yet death haunts their feet.
Almost as if all their knowledge cannot save them.
So do you see a showcase of power, or the skull waiting below?

meta.title: The Hidden Skull in Holbein's The Ambassadors
meta.description: Hans Holbein painted two wealthy diplomats in 1533 surrounded by scientific symbols. Hidden at their feet is an anamorphic skull representing mortality.
